params.body:
The link at the foot of every newsletter led to a page that could only unsubscribe from everything. With two newsletters, someone who no longer wants one of them would lose both.

**The page behind the link**

- It shows the two newsletters, Afrodidact and KUBO, each with a line about what it is, ticked as the person gets them, and the address they get them at.
- Untick one, tick the other, and save. "Unsubscribe from everything" takes them off the list.
- Someone who had unsubscribed sees both unticked and can tick one to come back. The link came to their own address, so that is them.
- Opening the page still changes nothing; only a button does, so a mail program that opens links to check them cannot change anything.
- In Dutch, French or English, after the language of the person.

**The call behind it**

`/api/newsletter-unsubscribe` takes `afrodidact` and `kubo` as true or false. Without them it unsubscribes from everything, as before.

**Checked**

- `npm test`, `npm run build`.
- In Chromium with a stand-in for Sanity: 12 steps (opening changes nothing, both ticked for someone on both, only one after unticking, unsubscribe from everything, coming back by ticking one, the old call, an unknown link, no sideways scroll on a phone).
params.title: Behind the link at the foot of a newsletter, readers choose which newsletters they get
